Here's a clean, production-style implementation using a **hash map + doubly linked list**, which is the standard approach to achieve O(1) `get` and `put`:

```python
class Node:
    def __init__(self, key=0, value=0):
        self.key = key
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None

class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.cache = {}  # O(1) key -> Node lookup
        
        # Sentinel nodes avoid null checks at boundaries
        self.head = Node()  # Marks most-recently-used end
        self.tail = Node()  # Marks least-recently-used end
        self.head.next = self.tail
        self.tail.prev = self.head

    def get(self, key: int) -> int:
        if key not in self.cache:
            return -1
        node = self.cache[key]
        self._move_to_head(node)  # Promote to most recently used
        return node.value

    def put(self, key: int, value: int) -> None:
        if key in self.cache:
            # Update existing entry and mark as recently used
            self.cache[key].value = value
            self._move_to_head(self.cache[key])
        else:
            new_node = Node(key, value)
            self.cache[key] = new_node
            self._add_to_head(new_node)  # Insert at most-recent position
            
            if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
                # Evict LRU item (node just before tail sentinel)
                lru = self.tail.prev
                self._remove(lru)
                del self.cache[lru.key]

    def _remove(self, node):
        """Unlink a node from the list in O(1)."""
        node.prev.next = node.next
        node.next.prev = node.prev

    def _add_to_head(self, node):
        """Insert node right after head sentinel."""
